summary: The r22 weighted section functional J_y0(g)=int sqrt(H(y)m(y)) |y-y0|^{-1/2}dy is not uniformly bounded even when (Y,Z) is an exact two-dimensional orthogonal projection of independent cap-one original coordinates. Take X1 with density the indicator of a measure-one union of intervals I_k=[3k,3k+delta_k], delta_k proportional to 1/[k(log k)^2], X2 uniform on [0,1], and Y=(X1+X2)/sqrt(2), Z=(X1-X2)/sqrt(2). Then ||p_(Y,Z)||_infinity=1 but J_0=infinity because the plateau contributions are bounded below by a constant multiple of 1/(k log k). Adding an independent X0 uniform on [0,1], the corresponding target quadratic form X0^2+2YZ equals X0^2+X1^2-X2^2 and has density <=pi by the diagonal beta argument. Thus this is not a QFORM counterexample; it proves the section-functional route loses essential original-product cancellation and must be replaced by a preimage-level curved aggregation.

partner_result_applied.application: For the exact 2x2 orthogonal projection (Y,Z), both physical row leverages equal one, so the theorem gives ||p_(Y,Z)||_infinity<=1; the constructed density attains this cap while the weighted section functional diverges.
